title: [P0] Complete service mesh freeze — all requests hanging indefinitely

failure.root_cause_statement: a distributed lock contention created a circular wait: service-a holds lock L1 and waits for lock L2, service-b holds lock L2 and waits for lock L3, service-c holds lock L3 and waits for lock L1, creating a system-wide deadlock that causes all three services to hang indefinitely since lock-manager has no deadlock detection timeout configured

correct_actions.message: lock-manager restarted. Lock table cleared — all deadlocked locks released. service-a, service-b, service-c resuming normal operation. Lock table rebuilt with default lock_ttl=30000ms.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Lock manager restarted. Lock table cleared. Active locks: 0. Default lock_ttl: 30000ms.
[{ts}] Lock L1 acquired successfully. Order processing resumed. Backlog: {val} orders draining.
[{ts}] Upstream services recovering. Success rate: {val}%. Timeout rate dropping.

partial_actions.message: Deadlock detection enabled. DEADLOCK DETECTED: circular wait L1(service-a) → L2(service-b) → L3(service-c) → L1. However, existing locks not auto-released — lock_ttl=0 prevents expiry. Services remain hung. Restart lock-manager or release_all_locks to break deadlock.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] DEADLOCK DETECTED: L1(held:service-a, waiting:service-c) → L2(held:service-b, waiting:service-a) → L3(held:service-c, waiting:service-b). Circular wait confirmed.
[{ts}] Auto-resolution blocked: lock_ttl=0 (disabled). Restart lock-manager or use release_all_locks to clear.

partial_actions.message: All locks force-released. Deadlock broken. service-a, service-b, service-c acquiring new locks and resuming. WARNING: Some in-flight transactions may need reconciliation.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Force-released {val} locks. Deadlock broken.
[{ts}] Lock L1 re-acquired. Processing resumed.

partial_actions.message: Traffic drained from api-router. No new requests entering. Existing deadlocked requests still hung in service-a, service-b, service-c. The deadlock is not resolved — only new traffic is stopped.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Traffic drain active. Incoming requests: 0/min. Hung requests in backend: {val} still waiting.

trap_actions.message: service-a restarted. On startup it immediately tries to acquire lock L1 from lock-manager — but L1 is still held in the deadlocked lock table. service-a hangs again within 3 seconds. Additionally, restart dropped {val} in-flight orders causing data inconsistency.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Service restarted. Attempting to re-acquire lock L1...
[{ts}] Lock L1 acquisition BLOCKED — still held by previous deadlocked session. Service hung again immediately.
[{ts}] CRITICAL: {val} in-flight orders lost during restart. Data reconciliation required.

trap_actions.message: service-b restarted but immediately re-deadlocks on lock L2 (still held in lock-manager). Restart dropped in-flight inventory reservations causing overselling risk.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Service restarted. Attempting lock L2...
[{ts}] Lock L2 BLOCKED — deadlocked. Service hung again. {val} inventory reservations lost.

trap_actions.message: service-c restarted but re-deadlocks on lock L3. Pending payment captures dropped.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Lock L3 BLOCKED — deadlocked. Service hung again after restart.

trap_actions.message: lock-manager scaled to multiple replicas. New replica joins the same lock table — deadlocked state is in shared storage, not in process memory. Scaling doesn't help. WORSE: split-brain risk introduced — two lock-managers may issue conflicting lock grants.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] CRITICAL: Split-brain detected — multiple lock-manager instances with divergent lock tables. Lock grants may conflict.

trap_actions.message: Circuit breakers reset to CLOSED. Traffic now flowing back to deadlocked services — all requests immediately hang, piling up in thread pools. Request queue grows unbounded. Memory pressure increasing on all services.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] All circuits reset to CLOSED. Probing upstream services...
[{ts}] All probes HANGING. Queued requests: {val}. Memory pressure: HIGH.

default_response.message: Action completed but had no observable effect on the deadlock. The circular lock dependency between service-a, service-b, and service-c persists in lock-manager.

red_herrings.description: circuit-breaker-proxy opens all circuit breakers after 30 seconds of upstream timeouts, producing a cascade of CIRCUIT_OPEN alerts that make it appear the services themselves are crashing or overloaded when they are actually deadlocked waiting for locks

api-router shows 100% request timeout rate and logs suggest it is dropping all connections, making it look like the router is misconfigured or overloaded — it is healthy but all requests hang waiting for the deadlocked services

service-b is the most visible hung service because it sits in the middle of the dependency chain and both service-a and service-c reference it in their timeout logs — but all three services are equally deadlocked

title: [P1] API gateway health checks failing — file descriptor exhaustion

failure.root_cause_statement: api-gateway is leaking file descriptors because a middleware added in v8.1.0 opens connections to config-service on every request but never closes them when the request errors, causing the FD limit of 65536 to be reached over 6 hours of gradual accumulation and making the gateway unable to accept new connections

correct_actions.message: api-gateway rolled back from v8.1.0 to v8.0.3. The leaking middleware has been removed. FD count dropping as leaked connections to config-service are cleaned up by kernel TCP timeout. Service accepting new connections.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Rolled back to v8.0.3. Middleware pipeline reverted. Open FDs: {val} (dropping — leaked connections timing out).
[{ts}] api-gateway backend healthy again. Traffic resuming.
[{ts}] Active connections dropping: {val}. CLOSE_WAIT sockets clearing.

partial_actions.message: api-gateway restarted. FD table reset to 0 — service is accepting connections again. WARNING: v8.1.0 is still deployed. The middleware connection leak will resume immediately. FDs will re-exhaust in approximately 6 hours.

post_logs.template: [{ts}] Service restarted. Open FDs: {val}/65536. Accepting connections.
[{ts}] v8.1.0 still active. FD leak rate: ~{val}/min from middleware → config-service. FDs will re-exhaust in ~6h.
[{ts}] api-gateway backend recovered. Traffic flowing.

partial_actions.message: Idle connections closed on api-gateway. Freed ~20000 FDs. However, new requests continue leaking FDs through the v8.1.0 middleware. This buys approximately 2 hours before re-exhaustion.

title: [P0] Intermittent 50% failure rate — service mesh connectivity broken

failure.root_cause_statement: dns-resolver CoreDNS config was updated by an operator to add a custom stub zone for svc-beta.internal that points to a stale IP address from a previous deployment, causing exactly 50% of DNS lookups for svc-beta to resolve to the old unresponsive pod IP while the other 50% hit the correct pod, producing a persistent ~50% error rate that appears to be a load-balancing or service degradation issue

title: [P1] Reporting API queries running 50x slower after maintenance window

correct_actions.message: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_events_user_created_at ON analytics.events(user_id, created_at) started. Building index on 2.1B rows — this will take 15-25 minutes but queries will progressively switch to index scans as the build completes. Sequential scans stopping.

partial_actions.message: Migration v204 rolled back. However, the rollback script only re-creates idx_events_user_created_at_bak (the backup index), not the original idx_events_user_created_at.
